citations.F1: N+1 query: `serialize_event` does one `actor_id` `fetchrow` per event — 1,912 sequential round-trips for acme; batch-fetch all actors in one `WHERE id = ANY($1)` query
citations.F2: dedups with an O(n²) `in seen` list scan ... or at minimum use a set for `seen`
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` uses synchronous `requests.get()` inside an async handler — it blocks the entire event loop ... switch to an async HTTP client (httpx) or run it in a thread pool
citations.F4: no index on `events(org_id, created_at)` — every call is a sequential scan over 4.2M rows; add a composite index (`org_id, created_at DESC`)
citations.F5: Same leak pattern in `_request_timings` — appended on every request, never trimmed; bound it (ring buffer or periodic reset)
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is an unbounded module-level dict that never evicts — it grows for the life of the pod; cap it or use a TTL/LRU cache
citations.F9: 16 workers × 50 conns × 6 pods = up to 4,800 Postgres connections ... This is also why just adding workers won't fix the freeze — more blocked event loops, not more throughput. ... Only after 2–7 are in: re-measure latency and pod RSS; then decide if a modest worker/pool bump or the response cache is still worth adding
citations.F11: `since` defaults to `datetime.now(timezone.utc) - 30d`, computed fresh to the microsecond on every request with no `since` param ... bucket/round the default window before using it as a cache key
